Six animals per arm received cinnamon or ginger aqueous extract alone or together in a streptozotocin-diabetes model. Combined extracts increased open-arm duration from 11.99 to 17.80 seconds versus untreated diabetic rats, p=0.004. The separate arms rose without significant comparisons. The combined arm also decreased closed-arm entries, a measure that can depend on activity. The individual arms and combination must remain separate. The rodents had diabetes rather than parkinsonism, the exposure was gavaged extract, and plus-maze behavior differs from clinical anxiety. The combination does not isolate either culinary ingredient.

MPTP mice received intravenous free curcumin or intravenous ferric-curcumin coordination polymers, with separate saline and levodopa arms. The formulated compound had the strongest pole, open-field and rotarod findings. Free curcumin produced only slight favorable rotarod changes as reported. Route, formulation and endpoint prevent attribution to eating ground turmeric.
